prompt: Read the English sentence: 'Not all students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) All students passed, (b) No student passed, or (c) At least one student passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
note: Option-order probe. A content-sensitive answer uses correct_choice; a position-sensitive answer uses original_correct_choice.

prompt: A speaker said: 'Some of the cookies were eaten.' What is the speaker most likely communicating? (a) No cookies were eaten, (b) At least one cookie was eaten, and possibly all of them, or (c) At least one cookie was eaten, but not all of them.
note: Option-order probe. A content-sensitive answer uses correct_choice; a position-sensitive answer uses original_correct_choice.

prompt: Read the sentences: 'Every student read some book. It was the same book for everyone.' Which reading does the continuation force? (a) Each student read a book, and the books may differ, (b) There is one book that every student read, or (c) No student read a book.
note: Option-order probe. A content-sensitive answer uses correct_choice; a position-sensitive answer uses original_correct_choice.
